_comment: Pinned descriptor AND provenance for the Oniro distribution HAP set.
This single committed file is the Eclipse Bucket-4a provenance: per app it
pins git + branch + sha (source-repo / source-sha), the global build_cmd, and
the license. build-oniro-haps.sh consumes it to CLONE each app from its pinned
remote into out/oniro-haps/src/<app> and build that, so the release is
reproducible from upstream (not from local working-tree state).
SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH: the colocated BUILD.gn also reads this file
(read_file at gn-gen time) and generates one ohos_prebuilt_etc per module
from 'dest' + 'install_dir' (target name = dest with .hap -> _hap). There is
no per-app gating: oniro_install_custom_haps takes the whole list or none of
it. Renaming these keys is a BUILD.gn interface change.
The built HAP binaries are NOT committed (see haps/.gitignore); only this file
is. A signed HAP is not bit-reproducible (hapsigner nonce) and Eclipse does not
redistribute it, so no per-HAP sha256 is pinned here; the driver writes
haps/SHA256SUMS (gitignored) for local verification.
'output' is the EXACT signed-HAP filename hvigor emits for that module (an
infix may disambiguate the wanted variant from co-built ones). Signing is
deterministic and host-independent: the driver nulls
each app's embedded signingConfig (encrypted passwords tied to per-machine
DevEco material fail off-host), builds the UNSIGNED hap, then signs with the
public OpenHarmony test keys (developtools/hapsigner, password 123456) at the
app's 'apl'; bundle name comes from each module's install_dir. An app with
'self_signed': true opts out of all of that and keeps its own signingConfig,
for apps whose committed signing material works off-host and whose exact
certificate or provision profile must be preserved.
WIRING: BUILD.gn's group('oniro_custom_haps') is listed in the product's
bundle.json sub_component (vendor/oniro/hybris_generic). No
applications/standard/hap patch is needed for the ADD-ON apps. The camera is
the exception: it replaces a stock hap installing the same path, so a
one-line product-scoped patch there drops camera_hap under the same gn arg.
The set is OPT-IN: BUILD.gn
generates no targets unless oniro_install_custom_haps=true (oniro_haps.gni),
and preinstall-config only adds the matching BMS entries in that case.
LICENSING / RELEASE SCOPE: the default product build installs none of the
apps below, so the release redistributes no Oniro-built HAP and their
licences are not the product's to satisfy. The app store is
GPL-3.0-or-later, which is why shipping it by default was withdrawn: it is
incompatible with the Apache-2.0 posture of the product image. Anyone who
opts in with oniro_install_custom_haps=true becomes the distributor of the
resulting image and takes on the obligations of every licence listed here.

apps.name: appstore
apps.license_evidence: LICENSE at the pinned sha is the GPLv3 text; source headers carry the FSF 'either version 3 of the License, or (at your option) any later version' grant. Upstream copyright: westinyang (https://gitee.com/ohos-dev).

apps.name: florisboard
apps.license_evidence: UNCONFIRMED. The pinned tree carries NO LICENSE file; its README states only that upstream FlorisBoard is Apache-2.0 and that the port 'keeps the same license for the reused data'. A LICENSE file must be added to the source repository before this app can be treated as Apache-2.0 licensed.

apps.name: camera
apps.license_evidence: Fork of applications/standard/camera (eclipse-oniro-mirrors/applications_camera); LICENSE at the pinned sha is Apache-2.0, and the fork adds only the rotation fix on top of upstream.
apps.build_cmd: hvigorw assembleHap --mode module -p module=phone@default -p product=default -p buildMode=release --no-daemon
apps._note: Replaces the STOCK com.ohos.camera instead of adding an app, so applications/standard/hap drops camera_hap under the same gn arg -- both install app/com.ohos.camera/Camera.hap. 'self_signed': true keeps the app's own signingConfig instead of the null-and-resign path: it commits working signing material (signature/OpenHarmony.p12 + camera.p7b) whose profile is an 'os_integration' one carrying a Camera distribution certificate that the generic UnsgnedReleasedProfileTemplate cannot reproduce, and com.ohos.camera has an app_signature entry in install_list_capability.json granting allowAppUsePrivilegeExtension, so the chain must stay byte-identical to the stock hap's (leaf 'OpenHarmony Application Release', SHA256 0716E4E8C9B8CEEF6A974CD2289D5C4C668A5B41FA5DF8C0542DCB72602371F5). The per-app 'build_cmd' targets the one module that ships (phone) and forces release mode; a debug build carries ets/sourceMaps.map and an unoptimised modules.abc and comes out ~9 MB larger.
